newsitem.title: UK: EMU moves musn't hurt bondholder rights - BOE group.
newsitem.headline: EMU moves musn't hurt bondholder rights - BOE group.

text.p: Bondholder rights should not be limited by any changes or redenomination of non-government debt as a result of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), a Bank of England-sponsored group said on Thursday.

"The group argues that it should be left for issuers and investors to decide whether to redenominate non-government debt securiities after stage three (of EMU) begins, and that bondholders rights should not be limited in any way," the group said in a report released by the Bank of England (BOE).
Stage three of EMU, under which the euro is to be introduced, is due to start on January 1, 1999.

"If issuers and investors decide to redenominate a particular issue, the group recommends that one of a very limited number of standard methods should be used in order to avoid confusion," the report said.
If Britain stays out of a single currency, the group said it saw a case for maintaining present British conventions where they are aligned with best international practice.
It said this "even if they would be different from those adopted in the euro area".

The report said the findings reflect the consensus of the group and that its recommendations "were broadly endorsed by all those who participated". The Bank said the group had its encouragement and chairmanship.

"On market conventions, the group considers that stage three of EMU provides an opportunity to harmonise conventions on new euro denominated securities across the euro area, and that this is a desireable goal," the report said.,

"There would be particular advantage in harmonising on best international practice. Existing issues should be allowed to run off, however, without their terms being changed, unless they are voluntarily converted in the market," the report said.

The group recommended an interest day count of Actual/360 in the euro money market and Actual/Actual in the euro bond markets, and that business days in these markets should be based on TARGET operating days (or feewer days by agreement.
The group was not yet able to identify a consensus on annual or semi-annual coupon frequency, the report said.

The group also arguyed for a single LIBOR (London Interbank Offered Rate) for the euro to be posted and the same rate used as LIBOR for each of the participating national currency units, in order to preserve continuity.
